# Type-Safe Computer Vision

> A three-part series by Thomas Stephan on computer vision bugs that are
> really type bugs, and on what it takes to make them unrepresentable. Each
> post takes one mistake that ships in production everywhere, measures it, and
> then shows the same operation written so that a compiler refuses the wrong
> version. The library the examples use is fovea, a Rust crate by the same
> author.

Prose and figures are copyright Thomas Stephan, all rights reserved. Code
snippets are MIT or Apache-2.0, matching fovea. Quote and link freely; please
attribute, and please do not reproduce the prose wholesale.

## Posts

- [The Blue Face Bug](https://karhunen-loeve.github.io/01-rgb-bgr-the-blue-face-bug.html):
  Three bytes in memory do not say which channel comes first. Read as RGB they
  are a warm skin tone, read as BGR they are ice blue. Why channel-order
  confusion is a type error rather than a logic error, and what the compiler
  can do about it once the pixel type records its own layout.

- [128 Is Not the Middle](https://karhunen-loeve.github.io/02-gamma-blind-interpolation.html):
  The average of a black and a white pixel is not 128. Stored bytes are a
  compressed code for light, so 128 carries roughly a fifth of the light and
  the correct answer is 188. This breaks every naive resize, blur and blend,
  and it has been re-discovered in Pillow, imgproxy, darktable, libvips and
  others for two decades. The post measures the error on a real photograph and
  shows the type distinction that prevents it.

## Tools

- [Browser tools](https://karhunen-loeve.github.io/tools/): pages that run the
  library in the reader's own browser, compiled to WebAssembly, with no upload
  and no network request after load.

- [FAST corners](https://karhunen-loeve.github.io/tools/fast-corners.html):
  the FAST segment test, interactive. Drop an image, move the threshold and the
  arc length, click a detected corner and read the sixteen ring samples that
  decided it.

## Optional

- [Atom feed](https://karhunen-loeve.github.io/feed.xml)
- [fovea on crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/fovea) and
  [on GitHub](https://github.com/karhunen-loeve/fovea): the library the posts
  are about.
- [fovea-examples](https://github.com/karhunen-loeve/fovea-examples): the
  programs that generated the figures, so any number in the posts can be
  reproduced.
